title: CLAT Practice Set 2
pageDesc: Free CLAT practice paper set 2 with detailed solutions.

questions.text: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which body acts as the adjudicatory authority for data‑privacy violations and can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore?

options.label: A
options.text: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)

options.label: B
options.text: Competition Commission of India (CCI)

options.label: C
options.text: Data Protection Board of India (DPBI)

options.label: D
options.text: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Data Protection Board of India (DPBI).

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following best describes an implicit assumption in an argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A stated reason supporting the claim.

options.label: B
options.text: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold.

options.label: C
options.text: A counterargument presented for refutation.

options.label: D
options.text: A statistical evidence cited by the author.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold..

questions.text: A candidate encounters an inference question where one option is factually true in the real world but not supported by the passage. According to the Principle of Passage‑Only Reasoning, how should this option be treated?

options.label: A
options.text: Select it because it is factually correct

options.label: B
options.text: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage

options.label: C
options.text: Select it if it aligns with the candidate's domain knowledge

options.label: D
options.text: Mark it as correct only if the passage does not contradict it

questions.solution: Correct answer: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage.

questions.text: Paragraph 1 cites a single study showing a 12% rise in test scores after a policy change. Paragraph 3 reveals the study had a small sample and short duration. The author concludes the policy is universally effective. This conclusion is:

options.label: A
options.text: Supported by the evidence presented.

options.label: B
options.text: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later.

options.label: C
options.text: Irrelevant to the study’s findings.

options.label: D
options.text: Strengthened by the later paragraph’s details.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later..

questions.text: Which case established that judicial review of constitutional amendments is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution, leading to the striking down of a clause that sought to curtail such review?

options.label: A
options.text: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)

options.label: B
options.text: Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967)

options.label: C
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

options.label: D
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980).

questions.text: The Government announces a policy to regularize all ad-hoc employees with 10 years of service. Relying on this, an employee declines a private job offer. Before regularization, the Government withdraws the policy citing fiscal constraints, without hearing the employee. The employee challenges the withdrawal. Which principle governs the outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The employee has a substantive right to regularization because the policy created a legitimate expectation enforceable as a contract.

options.label: B
options.text: The withdrawal is valid because legitimate expectation is merely a moral claim with no legal enforceability against the State.

options.label: C
options.text: The withdrawal is invalid because legitimate expectation requires a hearing before frustration, unless overriding public interest is shown, which mere fiscal constraints may not satisfy.

options.label: D
options.text: The employee can claim damages for breach of promise under promissory estoppel, but cannot compel regularization.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The withdrawal is invalid because legitimate expectation requires a hearing before frustration, unless overriding public interest is shown, which mere fiscal constraints may not satisfy..

questions.text: The government issues a press release stating that it will provide a 20 % subsidy to manufacturers of solar panels. Relying on this announcement, a company invests ₹5 crore in a new production line. Before any formal notification or scheme is published, the government withdraws the announcement. The company claims a legitimate expectation. What factual element is essential for the claim to succeed?

options.label: A
options.text: The announcement must be made in a formal gazette notification.

options.label: B
options.text: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation.

options.label: C
options.text: The government must have acted in bad faith when withdrawing the announcement.

options.label: D
options.text: The subsidy must be a statutory entitlement rather than a discretionary policy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation..

questions.text: What is the typical host arrangement for UN International Days?

options.label: A
options.text: A single permanent host country

options.label: B
options.text: Host rotates annually among member states

options.label: C
options.text: Host is always the UN headquarters in New York

options.label: D
options.text: Host is selected by the Secretary‑General for a five‑year term

questions.solution: Correct answer: Host rotates annually among member states.

questions.text: A constitutional amendment is challenged on the ground that it destroys the federal character of the Constitution by converting States into mere administrative units. The Supreme Court strikes down the amendment. Which maxim correctly captures the legal consequence and the doctrinal basis for this outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The amendment is voidable under the doctrine of eclipse, as it is inconsistent with fundamental rights.

options.label: B
options.text: The amendment is void ab initio under the basic structure doctrine, as it violates constitutional supremacy.

options.label: C
options.text: The amendment is ultra vires the legislative competence of Parliament under Article 368.

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment is intra vires but inoperative under the principle of severability until the federal structure is restored.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The amendment is void ab initio under the basic structure doctrine, as it violates constitutional supremacy..

questions.text: Parliament passes a constitutional amendment that removes the power of judicial review over all economic legislation, leaving only a limited appellate review. The amendment is challenged on the ground that it violates the basic structure of the Constitution. According to the basic structure doctrine as developed in Indian jurisprudence, what is the correct outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The amendment is valid because Parliament’s plenary power under Article 368 permits any amendment.

options.label: B
options.text: The amendment is invalid because judicial review is a basic feature of the Constitution and cannot be removed even for a limited domain.

options.label: C
options.text: The amendment is valid because it only curtails judicial review in a specific policy area, not the entire power.

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment is invalid only if it also alters the identity of the Constitution’s preamble.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The amendment is invalid because judicial review is a basic feature of the Constitution and cannot be removed even for a limited domain..

questions.text: The passage lists several common traps in advanced reading comprehension. Which of the following is explicitly identified as a trap?

options.label: A
options.text: Confusing the author's tone with the tone of a cited expert.

options.label: B
options.text: Over-inferring from limited evidence.

options.label: C
options.text: Failing to identify the main idea of each paragraph.

options.label: D
options.text: Misreading complex vocabulary.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Over-inferring from limited evidence..

questions.text: The Supreme Court declares a regulatory regime governing telecom licences unconstitutional but expressly states that all licences already granted under the regime shall remain valid until their expiry. The Court invokes a doctrine that limits the effect of its declaration to future cases. Which doctrine is being applied?

options.label: A
options.text: Doctrine of Prospective Overruling

options.label: B
options.text: Doctrine of Severability

options.label: C
options.text: Doctrine of Eclipse

options.label: D
options.text: Doctrine of Harmonious Construction

questions.solution: Correct answer: Doctrine of Prospective Overruling.

questions.text: A State Legislature enacts a law imposing a tax on "services rendered by way of legal consultation". The State argues it falls under Entry 62 (taxes on professions) of the State List. The Union argues it encroaches on Entry 97 (residuary power) or constitutes a tax on services (GST domain). The Court finds the true nature of the levy is a tax on the profession of advocates. Which maxim resolves this competence dispute?

options.label: A
options.text: Colourable legislation — the State has misused its power by labelling a service tax as a profession tax.

options.label: B
options.text: Pith and substance — the true character of the legislation determines its legislative competence.

options.label: C
options.text: Ultra vires — the State lacks any power to tax legal services under the Seventh Schedule.

options.label: D
options.text: Basic structure — federalism is violated if States tax professional services exclusively regulated by the Bar Council.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pith and substance — the true character of the legislation determines its legislative competence..

questions.text: A CLAT principle quotes Article 21 and adds: "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law, and such procedure must be fair, just, and reasonable." The facts state the government impounded a citizen's passport without giving him a hearing or stating reasons. Which option correctly applies the principle?

options.label: A
options.text: The action is valid because Article 21 only protects life, not the right to hold a passport.

options.label: B
options.text: The action is invalid because the procedure lacked fairness, justice, and reasonableness by denying a hearing.

options.label: C
options.text: The action is valid because impounding a passport is an administrative act not subject to judicial review.

options.label: D
options.text: The action is invalid only if the citizen can prove the government acted with mala fide intent.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The action is invalid because the procedure lacked fairness, justice, and reasonableness by denying a hearing..
